title: Running JavaScript and Understanding Values
summary: Learn how a JavaScript engine evaluates statements, how `const` and `let` bind names, and how to inspect values and runtime errors.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the JavaScript behavior taught in Running JavaScript and Understanding Values
Test behavior using observable output and assertions
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: JavaScript executes statements through an engine in a browser or Node.js. Prefer `const` when a binding will not be reassigned and `let` when reassignment is part of the design; avoid `var` in new beginner code because function scope and hoisting are easy to misread. A variable holds a value with a runtime type. Use `console.log` and `typeof` to inspect evidence. Read an error from its name and first relevant stack frame instead of guessing. `ReferenceError` commonly indicates an unavailable name, while `TypeError` means an operation was not supported by the received value.
keyPoints: JavaScript executes statements through an engine in a browser or Node.js.
commonMistakes: const does not make a referenced object deeply immutable

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Create a `.js` file.
2. Predict each output.
3. Run it in Node.js or a browser console.
4. Change one value.
5. Explain the observed change.
6. Add an assertion for the intended behavior.
